newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-PERU, MEXICO OPEN U.S. CUP TOURNAMENT WITH WINS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU, MEXICO OPEN U.S. CUP TOURNAMENT WITH WINS.

text.p: Defending champions Mexico defeated Denmark 3-1, while Peru spoiled opening night for the hosts with a 1-0 victory over the United States in the kick-off matches for the U.S. Cup soccer tournament Friday.
German Carty's goal in the eighth minute provided the only scoring in the opening match at Jack Murphy Stadium as Peru thwarted several U.S. threats in the second half to hang on to victory.
In the second game, Mexico dominated possession by passing the ball wide to the flanks. But Denmark clogged the middle to prevent any scoring chances.
Not until the Danes began to man-mark more tightly in the 30th minute did the middle of the field open for the Mexicans, who scored the first goal in the 40th minute.
Benjamin Galindo, dribbling in the middle of the field, sent the ball to Enrique Alfaro, whose 30-metre shot passed over the left shoulder of goalkeeper Mogens Krogh.
Luis Hernandez gave Mexico a 2-0 lead in the 55th minute when he found the net from an awkward angle near the end line 15 metres out.
Denmark narrowed the deficit to 2-1 in the 64th minute on Brian Steen Nielsen's 27-metre drive, but Mexico's Carlos Hermosillo converted in the 73rd minute to finish the scoring.
Mexico featured eight veterans from the 1994 World Cup -- including Hermosillo, who has won the scoring championship in Mexico's First Division three of the past four seasons.
Denmark's roster had nine players who had never previously competed for the national team.
Denmark will play Peru Sunday, with Mexico and the United States meeting in the second game.
